text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Dedicated pool 'resv-prod-3' at 100% GPU utilization, request queue > 420, average token latency 980ms. Autoscaler attempted 3 allocations, last error: "quota_exceeded". Impacting reserved tenants.

Priya Rao: seeing the pager, I'm taking on-call. quick triage: is this noisy neighbor or true capacity leak? @Samir can you confirm pool topology?

Samir Shah: looking now. metrics show 4 tenants with consistent sustained traffic. one tenant (tenant-fledger) is 60% of pool and has a large batch workload. KV cache hit low. I also see repeated allocation failures: 
```
autoscaler: allocate_executor(resv-prod-3) -> error: cloud: insufficient_quotas: GPUs not available in region us-west-2
2026-03-15T02:45:12Z | attempt 3/3
```

Eli Turner: confirmed quota_exceeded coming from cloud provider, not our scheduler failing to place. provider is throttling new instance creation. we can't autoscale up until quota increases or we evict.

Zoe Kim: noisy tenant behavior: tenant-fledger spikes steady 12-min windows with large batch inference (>4k tokens) and disables caching via their client forced flags. that's killing shared KV cache locality.

Priya Rao: immediate mitigation plan (0-30m):
- throttle or queue back non-enterprise tenants on resv-prod-3 (limit concurrent requests)
- identify largest session(s) from tenant-fledger and ask CS to request workload smoothing OR temporarily evict their burst widgets
- enable fallback routing to resv-prod-2 (has 20% headroom) for enterprise tenants that allow cross-pool routing

Jordan Lee: pinging FinLedger (tenant-fledger) now — will ask them to pause heavy batch runs. ETA response 10m.

Nadia Ortiz: implementing throttling rules on the ingress LB for non-reserved traffic. command I'm applying: 
```
rbctl route update --pool resv-prod-3 --concurrency-limit 80 --priority enterprise
```

Samir Shah: I'm running an eviction of the largest non-enterprise workloads to free ~4 GPUs. running: 
```
rbctl reservation evict --pool resv-prod-3 --filter "tenant:non-reserved" --dry-run
rbctl reservation evict --pool resv-prod-3 --filter "tenant:non-reserved" --limit 2
```

Priya Rao: do NOT evict enterprise tenants. only targeted non-reserved starters.

incident-bot: [action] evict job queued (id: evict-197300-01). Estimated free GPUs: 4 in ~90s.

Eli Turner: in parallel I'm opening a cloud support ticket to request emergency GPU quota bump in us-west-2 and checking spare capacity in us-east-1 for cross-region failover. Ticket id: CLOUD-98732. ETA from provider unknown.

Zoe Kim: enabling degraded model variant for enterprise tenants that accept lower-cost variants — switching from base-large -> base-medium for select tenants. This reduces per-request GPU memory by ~40%. Patching routing policy now.

Samir Shah: eviction completed. freed 3 GPUs (below estimate). queue dropped from 420 -> 180 in ~60s. latency down to 640ms.

Priya Rao: good. which enterprise tenants still impacted? Jordan?

Jordan Lee: FinLedger reported ~60% of their requests are now in fallback route to resv-prod-2. They see sporadic 5xx on some streamed responses earlier but currently <1% error. Customer impact: degraded latency and partial routing to a different pool; no data loss.

Nadia Ortiz: ingress throttles in place and applied at edge for non-enterprise. Rule is reversible.

Samir Shah: note: autoscaler logs show repeated failed allocations caused by provider-side rate-limit (createVM: rate_limit_exceeded), not raw quota. that explains intermittent behaviour.

Priya Rao: action items (now -> 2h):
- Eli: chase CLOUD-98732 urgency, ask for immediate quota or regional placement exceptions. (owner: Eli)
- Samir: schedule a medium-term automated noisy-tenant mitigation (per-tenant batch cap) and add a detection alert. (owner: Samir)
- Zoe: confirm fallback routing for enterprise tenants is stable and document regression plan (owner: Zoe)
- Jordan: follow up with FinLedger on workload smoothing and offer temporary config to reduce batch sizes (owner: Jordan)
- Nadia: keep throttles and circuit breakers monitored, rollback plan ready. (owner: Nadia)

Eli Turner: update from cloud: provider acknowledges rate limits at account level for new GPU nodes. they propose a 2h window for quota increase. pushed for immediate exception.

Jordan Lee: FinLedger responded: they paused nightly bulk jobs and will throttle to 50% for next 3 hours. They appreciate the fallback routing.

Priya Rao: status check 30m: queue 180 -> 75, latency 430ms -> 300ms. impact narrowed to a few customers with sticky allocation.

Samir Shah: creating retrospective ticket: INF-7231 noisy-tenant-evictions + autoscaler-retry-hardening. Adding logs and commands used.

Zoe Kim: quick config note for postmortem: allow enterprise tenants opt-in to cross-pool fallback; default is opt-out. update proposal in product backlog.

Priya Rao: handoff to infra for next 2h monitoring window. I'll mark incident as mitigated for paging, but keep this thread open until cloud confirms quota bump or permanent mitigations are in place.

Eli Turner: accepted. monitoring runbook engaged, I'll post updates in this thread.

incident-bot: Incident state changed -> Mitigated (paging lifted). Severity: Sev2.

Priya Rao: thanks everyone. postmortem owners: Samir (root cause + detection), Zoe (fallback behavior + product change), Eli (cloud vendor escalation + quota management), Jordan (customer comms). We'll sync tomorrow 11:00 PT for RCA and follow-ups. :thumbsup:

Samir Shah: adding logs and timeline to INF-7231. dropping a sample of the autoscaler errors: 
```
2026-03-15T02:41:01Z autoscaler: attempt create node -> rate_limit_exceeded
2026-03-15T02:42:10Z autoscaler: attempt create node -> insufficient_quotas
2026-03-15T02:43:33Z autoscaler: attempt create node -> throttled by provider
```

Jordan Lee: will update FinLedger with mitigation summary and expected next steps after the RCA.

Nadia Ortiz: leaving throttles in place for 3h, will auto-revert if pool CPU/GPU < 65% for >15m.

Priya Rao: closing notes: no customer data exposure, impact = degraded latency / partial fallback for a subset of enterprise tenants. Next steps captured. Thanks all.
